sections.s1-scope: These rules apply to vessels holding a DEM-04 stock account on the north Gackwych grounds. Tonnages are stated in metric tonnes to two decimal places. Where a figure appears in correspondence and also in the allocation schedule, the allocation schedule governs. Rules are not applied retrospectively, and each rule is applied using the version in force when it is applied.
sections.s2-carry-over: On the last day of each allocation block, unused tonnage is calculated as total allowance for the block less the sum of valid recorded landings counted in that block. Carry-over into the next block is limited to the carry-over cap percentage of the base allocation for the block. Unused tonnage above that cap is forfeited. The cap percentage is the one set by the version in force on the last day of the block.
sections.s3-transfers: Leased-in tonnage is added to total allowance from its effective date and does not change the base allocation. Leased-out tonnage is deducted from total allowance from its effective date, but only where the transfer has been approved and has not been withdrawn before that date. Total allowance for a block is base allocation plus carry-over from the previous block plus leased-in tonnage in effect, less leased-out tonnage in effect.
sections.s4-voided-entries: A landing entry marked voided is excluded from recorded landings for every purpose, including carry-over and remaining allowance. Landing entries for any other stock account are never counted against DEM-04.
sections.s5-landing-declarations: The landing declaration is due within the window set by the version in force on the recorded landing date. The window is counted in clock hours from the recorded landing time to the time the declaration is received. A declaration received exactly at the end of the window is within time. Declarations received after the window are late and are referred to the Quota Management Unit.
sections.s6-designated-remote-points: A designated remote point is a landing point named in this section. Ceandfell Remote Landing Point was designated from 2025-09-01. Carport Quay is not a designated remote point, and no remote-point exception applies to landings made there.
sections.s7-version-rule: Each rule is applied using the version in force on the date the rule is applied. A carry-over is applied on the last day of its block. 1. SCOPE
1.1 This memo applies to every student enrolled on a course that uses simulator bays 1 to 4 at Hendgate Airfield.
1.2 It does not apply to type-rating blocks run under contract by Quemfrounex Aviation Academy. Those follow schedule QA-7.
1.3 Simulator bay 5 is out of service until further notice. Sessions booked in bay 5 are excluded from every count in this memo.
1.4 The fee card is issued separately by the records office and is not changed by this memo.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 Week: seven consecutive days from Monday to Sunday inclusive. A week is named by its Monday.
2.2 Instructional hour (ih): clock time in a simulator session with an instructor logged as present. Briefing and debrief time are not instructional hours. Briefing is recorded separately in brief minutes and is deducted from the session length. Time is counted in whole minutes and is never rounded.
2.3 Session block: all sessions for one student on one calendar day, read in time order, whichever bay they are flown in. A session block ends at any break of 20 minutes or more. Two sessions separated by a break of less than 20 minutes form one block.
2.4 Booked start: the start time shown in the timetable for a session or booking.
2.5 Notice: the period from the time a cancellation is logged in the cancellation register to the booked start. Notice is measured in hours and minutes and is not rounded to whole hours.
2.6 Stage: the training stage recorded on the student file on the date in question. A stage change takes effect from the date written on the stage sign-off.

3. ALLOWANCE RULES (VERSION 4, EFFECTIVE 2026-02-02)
3.1 Stage 1 students: no more than 8 ih in any week.
3.2 Stage 2 students: no more than 12 ih in any week.
3.3 Stage 3 students: no weekly cap.
3.4 No student may log more than 4 ih on one calendar day, whatever their stage.
3.5 A booking cancelled with notice of 24 hours or more is not counted against the weekly allowance. A booking cancelled with notice of less than 24 hours is counted at its full booked length, unless clause 3.6 applies.
3.6 Medical exception: a booking cancelled for a documented medical reason is not counted against the weekly allowance, provided a medical certificate covering the booked start date is on file by the third calendar day after that date. Day 1 is the calendar day after the booked start date, so day 3 is three calendar days after it.
3.7 A session cancelled by the school because of a simulator fault logged before the session starts is never counted against the student.
3.8 A student arriving late does not change the booked length. A session is counted at its booked length unless a rule in this memo says otherwise.

4. AMENDMENT A (EFFECTIVE 2026-04-13)
4.1 For Stage 2 students, the weekly cap in clause 3.2 is reduced from 12 ih to 10 ih.
4.2 Amendment A applies to every week beginning on or after 2026-04-13. Weeks beginning before 2026-04-13 remain under clause 3.2 as written in version 4.
4.3 Clauses 3.1, 3.3, 3.4 and 3.5 to 3.8 are not changed by Amendment A.
4.4 Amendment A was approved by the Hendgate standards panel on 2026-03-25. It requires no action from students.

8. CANCELLATION AND RECORD RULES
8.1 Reason codes: PER personal; MED medical; FLT simulator fault; SCH school cancellation.
8.2 Cancellations are entered in the cancellation register by the records office on the day they are received. The logged time is the time shown in the register, not the time the student first spoke to an instructor.
8.3 A medical certificate is filed against the cancellation reference, not against the student's general file. A certificate must state the student's fitness to attend the booked session.
8.4 Weekly totals are calculated from the session log each Sunday night. Totals are not adjusted for bookings already treated under clause 3.5 or clause 3.6.
8.5 Session logs and register entries are kept for 24 months after the student leaves the course.

9. APPEALS
9.1 A student may appeal an allowance decision within 14 days of the decision. Appeals go to the chief flying instructor in writing.
9.2 An appeal does not stop a count from being applied. Where an appeal succeeds, the correction is made at the next weekly total.

scheme.administered_by: Huxwuix Seed Certification Office, Froucombe Depot

clauses.text: Scope: this scheme covers wheat, barley, oats and rye grown from certified seed stock in the Huxwuix region, including the Froucombe and Feandness valleys.
Germination is the percentage of normal seedlings in a laboratory test on a sample drawn from the lot. A result equal to the class minimum meets that minimum.

Off-types are counted at field inspection. The off-type rate is off-type plants per 1,000 plants inspected, with off-types and plants inspected both summed across all field inspections of the same lot. A rate equal to the class maximum meets that maximum.

Isolation is the shortest distance in metres from the nearest edge of the crop to the nearest edge of any other crop of the same species. A distance equal to the class minimum meets that minimum. The base-class minimum is the one in force at the lot's sealing date, as set by the amendments list.
The seal is applied by the certification officer or an appointed inspector once the field file for the lot is complete. The sealing date is the date the seal is recorded in the field file.

scheme.eligibility_rule: Lines marked ineligible are removed from the claimed total before any match rate is applied. The remainder is the eligible cost.
